newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle futures close lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle futures close lower.

text.p: Expectations that cash fed cattle markets would trend lower in the next several weeks on increased supplies pressured most months of CME live and feeder cattle futures at the close, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.525 to 0.025 cent per lb lower with June off 0.275 at 65.450 cents. Feeder cattle finished up 0.250 to off 0.375 with only May up after setting a new high early of 76.600. August was off 0.350 at 77.150 cents.

Cash fed cattle prices are expected to work lower into June as increased numbers become available. Part of the concern was visible on trade expectations for Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report, some sources noted. Analysts generally expect the report to show larger-than-year-ago on-feed supplies.

Analysts' estimates for May 1 on-feed numbers in the seven major feeding states averaged 109.6 percent of a year ago and ranged from 108 to 111 percent. April placements averaged 113.9 percent of a year earlier and ranged from 104.9 to 127.5 while April marketings averaged 101.0 and ranged from 98.6 to 104 percent.
Refco, Cargill Investor Services and R.J. O'Brien were on both sides in June during the day. Late RBH bought June and sold August while ABN Chicogo Corp bought August and sold June, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought June 66 calls and June 64 and 65 puts. Volatility was up one percent to 10 percent in June, pit sources added.

May feeders held gains on recent strength in cash feeders, but deferred months retreated, depressed by a weaker tone to fed cattle prices and concern cattle feeders' profit margins will tighten as a result, traders said.
"We have real bad breakevens," one trader said citing the poor potential to hedge feeding margins at the current price levels of feeders and grains against live cattle.

A break in grain futures sparked support around midsession but only May held as sellers again cited an overbought market and potential for fed cattle prices to ease and demand for feeders to slip, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index advanced $0.68 to $75.97 per cwt, the highest level since January 26, 1995.
RBH, Refco and Cargill Investor Services sold August late. Smith Barney bought September, pit sources said.
